notes.2: Serves 12. Use the largest bowl you have.

move.title: Every cube the same
move.body: Israeli salad is cucumber, tomato, and pepper cut into tiny, even cubes and dressed with lemon and olive oil. There's nothing to hide behind: the dice is the dish. This is the unit's mastery cook, so you'll do every cut on your own.

callback.body: You've diced for pico: planks, sticks, cubes. Israeli salad uses the same cuts, finer and on more vegetables, and every cube shows in the bowl.

why.title: About ¼ inch
why.body: A fine dice is about ¼ inch on every side, the size of a pea. Small enough that each forkful gets some of everything, big enough that the cucumber still crunches.

why.title: Even planks make even cubes
why.body: The first cut decides the rest. If the planks are all ¼ inch thick, the sticks and cubes cut from them can't help being even.

why.title: Flat side down
why.body: A round cucumber or a curved pepper wall rocks under the knife. Cut it so a flat side sits on the board, and it stays put.

why.title: Dress it just before serving
why.body: Salt draws water out of cut cucumber and tomato. Dressed early, the salad sits in a puddle; dressed at the table, it stays crisp.

wrong.sign: The cucumber cubes are bigger than the tomato
wrong.fix: Cut the next cucumber planks a little thinner, and recut the big cubes once more.
Use firm tomatoes, and slide the blade forward through the skin instead of pressing down.
Drain it in the colander and dress it again. Next time, dress it right before it's eaten.

quiz.q: How big is a fine dice?
choices: About ¼ inch, the size of a pea
As small as a grain of rice
quiz.explain: A mince is the size of a grain of rice; a fine dice is a little bigger.

quiz.q: Why is the salad dressed right before serving?
choices: Salt draws water out and makes it soggy
Oil makes it hard to stir
quiz.explain: Dressed at the table, it stays crisp.

steps.text: Set the cutting board on a damp paper towel, hone the knife, and set out the large bowl. This is a mastery cook: an adult stays nearby but doesn't help with the cuts.
Peel the cucumbers in stripes, or leave the skin on. Cut each into 3-inch pieces, stand each piece on end, and slice it into planks ¼ inch thick.
steps.tip: Standing a piece on its cut end gives it a flat bottom.

steps.text: Lay the planks flat, cut them into ¼-inch sticks, then cut across the sticks into ¼-inch cubes. Put them in the bowl.
steps.look: Cubes the size of a pea, with seeds still in.

steps.text: Quarter the tomatoes and scoop out the seeds. Lay each quarter skin side down, cut ¼-inch strips, then cut across them into cubes. Add them to the bowl.
steps.tip: Slide the blade forward through the skin; don't press down.

steps.text: Cut the top and bottom off the pepper, cut down one side, and open it flat. Cut away the core and ribs. Lay it skin side down and cut ¼-inch strips, then cubes. Add them to the bowl.
Peel the red onion half, leaving the root on. Lay it flat side down and dice it fine, strips toward the root, then across. Add it to the bowl.
steps.look: Cubes a little smaller than the rest, since raw onion is strong.

steps.text: Dry the parsley well and mince it fine, rocking the knife with your hand flat on the spine. Add it to the bowl.
Look over the bowl. Recut any cube that's much bigger than the rest.
steps.look: Every vegetable in cubes about the same size.

steps.text: In the small bowl, whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper with the fork.
Right before serving, pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently with the spoon. Taste, and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
